_help: Policy knobs for the customer-support gate (sending an email to a customer). Every knob has a one-sentence why.
on_ezio_failure_why: Fail closed: an email can wait for a person, but a wrong price or policy sent to a customer can't be unsent; our own data check still runs and BLOCKs known contradictions during an outage.
tier_decisions_why: GREEN defers to our checks (it is not proof accuracy was checked: most wrong-fact drafts score GREEN with accuracy not_scored); YELLOW or RED means Ezio sees a real problem, so a person looks; BLOCK is reserved for proven contradictions below.
contradicted_claim_why: A claim Ezio's fact-check contradicts (for example about GDPR) is a proven falsehood our price sheet can't see, so the email must not go out (business rule 6).
unverifiable_claim_why: Ezio found a claim it could not verify either way: a person decides, because unverified is neither true nor false.

tone.why: Below 60 is Ezio's critical band; the mock costs at most 30 tone points for acronyms like EPS or USD, so only real hype (exclamations, shouting, hype words) gets here, which rule 4 says needs review.

bias.why: Below 60 means repeated one-sided framing ('clearly', 'everyone knows'), which is not how we talk to customers; single mild words are handled by our own wording rules instead.

agreement.why: Below 60 means repeated flattery ('you're absolutely right', 'great question'), the sign of agreeing with a customer instead of checking them (rule 4); one polite phrase stays above it.

when_accuracy_not_scored_why: 'Not scored' only means Ezio found no public-knowledge claims; our price-sheet check covers this persona's facts, and rule 5 says a missing accuracy score is not a reason to hold.
when_accuracy_unavailable_why: When the fact-check service is down, claims only Ezio can check (laws, regulations) go unchecked, so a person reviews instead of approving blind.
checker_error_why: If our own data check crashes, the gate holds rather than approving without its independent signal.
welfare_mode_why: The best-option check explains when a correct email still leaves the customer on a worse deal; it is advisory so it informs the reviewer without overriding the business rules the gate is held to ('enforce' turns it into a HOLD).
